bound_context.boundary_below: cc cc cc cc (int3 padding) immediately below 0x6248790
bound_context.version_note: the bundle pins zstd-sys 2.0.15+zstd.1.5.7 / 2.1.2+zstd.1.5.7 and this body is byte-identical in both, so the window fixes the behaviour but not the zstd revision

register_roles.r10: mEnd (preserved; reused as a scratch word in phase 2)

caller_census.contract: value-returning: all 56 call sites read the count - 44 fold it into arithmetic (add/sub/lea on rax, including 9 sites that use it as a memory base in `lea rX,[rax+4]`), 12 copy it into another register for later use, and 0 discard it

consumer_meaning.arithmetic: the count is folded into a running total, a length, or the base of an address computation
consumer_meaning.register-copy: the count is moved to another register and used later in the same FDE

observations.claim: vEnd is min(iEnd, ip + (mEnd - match)) computed with an UNSIGNED cmovbe at 0x62487a4
phase 1 counts the agreeing bytes of (ip, match) below vEnd and stops at the first difference
the wrap test is (match + len1 == mEnd) at 0x62487f3 / 0x624886f; without it phase 2 is skipped
phase 2 counts the agreeing bytes of (ip+len1, mStart) below iEnd, using r8 = mStart as its only match-side cursor
the return value is the input-side length: every exit computes cursor - ip
the first differing byte in a word comes from tzcnt at 0x62487e1/0x624881a/0x624889b/0x624894f, each guarded by a cmp/je on the same words
the whole-word loop requires ip < vEnd-7, the dword tail cursor < vEnd-3 and the word tail cursor < vEnd-1, so no read crosses vEnd
the byte tail advances by sete (0 or 1), so it stops at the first difference

the routine writes no caller memory: no instruction in the window has a memory destination, and the only memory writes are the two callee-saved spills (push rbp at 0x6248796, push rbx at 0x624879d), matched by four pops (0x6248825/0x6248826 on the first return path, 0x6248874/0x6248875 on the second) - the earlier wording 'no stores at all' was wrong because push writes memory
the body has no endbr64 and the four bytes below the window are cc cc cc cc
56 direct calls, 0 tail jumps, in a handful of large caller FDEs; every call site consumes the count
the phase-2 wrap models the dictionary tail ending at mEnd and the match continuing at the block start
the caller is responsible for ip+len1 never running past iEnd while phase 2 reads forward
a vEnd below 7 is unreachable for real pointers (memory is not mapped there), which is why the vEnd-7 wrap is unobservable
the routine is a static (non-indirectly-called) function, hence no CET landing pad

review_followups.finding: classify_rax_use skipped non-register operands, so %rax used as the base of a memory operand (lea rX,[rax+4]) was invisible and the scan ran on to an unrelated later write: 9 of 56 rows were misclassified (5 as 'overwritten', 4 with a wrong distance/class)
review_followups.resolution: census.py now detects the read through ins.regs_access(), which includes base/index registers; the recomputed census is arithmetic 44 / register-copy 12 / overwritten 0, matching the reviewer's independent re-derivation of all 56 rows. verify.py pins the 9 memory-base sites and asserts that every row's first use names a rax register (the previous 'all sites consume' check was a tautology), and the 'writes nothing' test now reads the decoded stream instead of the vacuous store capture.

review_followups.finding: the wrap sentence for a vEnd below 7 stated the wrong direction
review_followups.resolution: corrected: with a wrapped bound the unsigned jae is NOT taken and control enters the 8-byte loop (0x62487b1) instead of the byte tail; the wraparound is unreachable for real heap pointers and is recorded as an inference

unknowns: which of the 56 call sites are reachable for a given compression level or block size is not characterized
whether every caller keeps the pointer invariant (match >= mStart, mEnd <= the block end) is not verified from the call sites
the exact zstd revision is not pinned (the body is identical in the two bundled zstd-sys versions)
the geometry of the real dictionary tail (how often mEnd - mStart exceeds the 8-byte loop bound) is not measured
the three identical source objects are not individually identified; only 0x6248790 is bound
